quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Morgan Stanley’s 14th annual Laguna Conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur (75 days as a new company): the first two months of Q3 have been 'good or very good'; 'we feel confident that next few quarters continue to be upper end of 4%-6%, more towards 6%', with similar momentum in Q4 and a good setup for 2027; the $12 earnings goal for 2029 is 'more of a floor', and the growth algorithm carries 2% of bridge or contingency. CFO Mike Stepniak: short-cycle orders across the board are up high single digit for the first 2.5 months of the quarter and long-cycle book-to-bill has been 1.1, 1.2 for a while; price is about 4% right now, with price-cost neutral to slightly positive. CEO: industrial inflation persists at '3%-ish... even 4% in some segments' and he has no signal it will change in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: next few quarters upper end of 4%-6%; $12 EPS 2029 as a floor; 2% contingency; long-cycle book-to-bill 1.1, 1.2; price about 4%

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Morgan Stanley’s 14th annual Laguna Conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: 'Our backlog in Process Automation Technology is up 25%. That's historic high', positioning the segment for the second half of 2026 and for 2027; Honeywell is 'highly confident' of high single-digit Process Automation and Technology growth over the next six months on backlog conversion. Building Automation has been gaining share for multiple quarters, and Industrial Automation's share losses of 2025 and earlier are reversing, turning a shrinking business to modest growth.

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Morgan Stanley’s 14th annual Laguna Conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: Honeywell has identified eight high-growth markets (in buildings data centers, hospitals and hospitality; in process LNG and life sciences; semiconductors in Industrial) that are 20% of the mix today and growing at a rate of 15% in 2026, against 80% mature markets growing at a 3%-4% rate; the Investor Day goal is 25% of the mix - Honeywell expects to finish this year at 20%-21% and hopes for 21%-22% next year. Services and software are 40% of revenue with a 45% target; last year Honeywell built an Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system covering the installed base of its about 15 businesses to measure penetration. Forge revenue is about $1 billion of ARR, about 5% of revenue. Apart from the completed spins of Aerospace and Advanced Materials, Honeywell separated three businesses and acquired six.
quarterly_data.figure: high-growth verticals 20% of mix growing 15%; 25% mix target (20%-21% in 2026); services and software 40% of revenue (45% target)

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Morgan Stanley’s 14th annual Laguna Conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on data centers: automation content in a data hall is about 1.5%-2% of the capital; data centers are 'a little over 5%' of Building Automation and growing 'north of 20%, even higher' off a small base. Data centers have very recently started building their own power generation because of interconnection problems, so Process Automation can now play in the 'power island' beside Building Automation in the data hall, and Honeywell has 'active engagement with few data center builders who want both'; data-center build-out in Europe and early build-outs in Korea and India also benefit Honeywell's global footprint.
quarterly_data.figure: automation content about 1.5%-2% of data-hall capital; data centers a little over 5% of Building Automation, growing north of 20%

quarterly_data.quarter: Honeywell Morgan Stanley’s 14th annual Laguna Conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on LNG: growth rests on two acquisitions - the core heat-exchanger technology asset (gas to liquid) bought from Air Products and Sundyne special compressors; at the capacity the acquired businesses had, Honeywell is 'booked for till 2029, 2028, 2029', so 'We are expanding that capacity substantially... and that is mostly already deployed'. LNG demand was secular before the Iran war, which added demand for diversified supply; he expects the cycle to remain strong for at least the next three to four years.
quarterly_data.figure: LNG capacity booked till 2028, 2029; capacity expansion mostly deployed
